linkedin.title: Most people feel overwhelmed by the news, not informed.
linkedin.body:
It is easy to blame the algorithm for this, but the real problem is that we treat information consumption like a firehose. We scroll through everything, hoping that by sheer volume, we will somehow absorb what matters. It rarely works.

The truth is that we are all interested in different things. A software engineer, a small business owner, and a student have different priorities. When news is presented as a one-size-fits-all feed, it is bound to miss the mark for everyone.

Personalised news is not about filtering out the world to create an echo chamber. It is about filtering out the noise so you can actually engage with the topics that shape your specific life and work. When you cut through the clutter, you stop skimming and start understanding.

We built Headlinne to solve this. We use AI to help you find the stories that are relevant to you, not just the ones that generate the most clicks. It is a better way to stay sharp without the burnout.

beats.detail: Events unfolded across cities in France.
beats.narration: Here is how a mass protest turns into widespread chaos.

beats.caption: Massive crowds rally against rising costs across France.
beats.detail: Protests were reported across the country.
beats.narration: It started with half a million people marching against the cost of living.

beats.caption: The situation turned from marching to violent clashes.
beats.detail: Tensions escalated rapidly during the day.
beats.narration: But peaceful movement quickly shifted into something much more volatile and dangerous.

beats.caption: Reports show looting and fires breaking out citywide.
beats.detail: Disorder spread across multiple French cities.
beats.narration: Looting broke out in cities. Buildings were set on fire.

beats.caption: Authorities have confirmed over 1,000 arrests so far.
beats.narration: Police moved in to control the crowds. Over one thousand people were arrested.

beats.caption: The government faces rising pressure to restore order.
beats.detail: BBC World reported on the unfolding events.
beats.narration: This creates a difficult situation for the government to manage right now.

story_card.headline: Bank of England chief exits IMF meeting over Russia
story_card.standfirst: Andrew Bailey joined a protest against Russian involvement during a finance summit.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey walked out of an IMF meeting in Bangkok.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: The exit was a protest against the Russian finance minister speaking to the group.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: It shows finance leaders are using their presence to signal opposition to Russia.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Future international summits to see if these protests continue or escalate.

story_card.caption:
Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey walked out of an IMF meeting in protest against Russia.

Bailey was among several finance leaders who left the session as the Russian finance minister began to address the group. This move highlights the ongoing diplomatic tensions within global financial institutions.
